title: LED Inspection - Contamination Detection on WaferSight PWG
subtitle: Post-Implant Quality Validation for 65nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Wei Zhang

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the WaferSight PWG system to detect and classify Contamination defects during post-implant inspection at the 65nm technology node. The test is conducted at Singapore Fab 7 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Contamination defects that are critical to yield at the 65nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the WaferSight PWG platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: WaferSight PWG
- Inspection Type: LED Inspection
- Target Defect: Contamination
- Process Step: Post-Implant
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 65nm
- Fab Location: Singapore Fab 7

This test case applies to all WaferSight PWG systems deployed at Singapore Fab 7 for post-implant monitoring in the 65nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: WaferSight PWG
Software Version: v10.9.297
Recipe: LED_INSPECTION_65nm_POST_IMPLANT
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Low (83 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.25μm
Edge Exclusion: 5mm
Sampling Plan: 5-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the WaferSight PWG system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'LED Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Contamination defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 65nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 104 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 94% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.6% for LED Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.93 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-05-17
Wafers Tested: 24
Total Defects Found: 1753
Defect Density: 248.0 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 6.8%
Capture Rate: 95.6%
Test Duration: 236 minutes
System Uptime: 97.7%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The WaferSight PWG demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Contamination at the 65nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Minor calibration drift was detected after extended run; re-calibration resolved the issue.

e) Statistical process control charts showed stable performance over the test period.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
